Dear Eleanor,

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 11 August 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular:

* Transcript of your conversation with Bolt Customer Support starting on 10 August 2024

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

Hi [~accountid:61a5f6316d002b006bce1fdc] we received the attached from our external counsel. [^BOLT_Contract Workers advice.23.08.24.FINAL.docx] and here is a summary: 

Ghana’s labour laws permit employers to hire workers through third party employment centres or private employment agencies. However, these centres or agencies must adhere to comprehensive guidelines outlined by the legislation, ensuring that they operate in compliance with the law.


Any references to supervision and management by in-house company resources in the contract should be replaced with detailed, measurable performance standards in the contracts. These should outline reporting requirements, including frequency and content, as well as clearly defined penalties or remedies if the agents fail to meet the agreed-upon standards.

It is essential to ensure that the relationship with the outsourced workers remains clearly within the bounds of a contract for services. This can be achieved by minimising control (without compromising on the standards or deliverables required by Bolt) over the workers' day-to-day activities, allowing them to operate with a level of autonomy that is consistent with that of independent contractors. Payments to the contractors should not be in the form of salaries, where tax deductions are made on a Pay As You Earn (PAYE)basis and pension payments deducted on a regular basis. Bolt should rather deduct withholding taxes from the services provided by the independent contractor. Additionally, even though the courts refer to the fact or the substance of the parties relationship and not only the contractual terms, clearly defining the terms of the engagement in the contract to show the independent relationship and regularly reviewing the working relationship can help prevent the misclassification of these workers.

Some outputs from research:

* One seemingly useful approach is trying to “overfit the model to get least error” (so that the model attributes all errors making the ads impact varying).
* Gaussian Processes can easily pick up different dynamic and produce very optimistic results. It can be solved by:
** working with priors on *ls* and *eta.* Giving them all the freedom will make them overlearn. Setting them to specific values is very strict. (This problem is specifically noticeable, when thinking about the approach “overlearn and see what’s the most extreme impact“). 
** one balance proposed can be:
*** setting ls=1 and giving eta some reasonable prior
*** set beta_counterfactual to Truncated normal / Uniform with some very specific lower bound (where you believe your ads impact can be).
* You can give all the freedom to eta and ls. But if you’re using HSGP, they will not be very flexible, unless you specify the M (in HSGP settings) to be big enough
* The model can produce weird results, if Android/iOS relations are not stable (e.g. Paris and Johannesburg). This can be fixed by introducing the trend (unless we’re sure that ads are generating this change). Ideally we also understand why this trend is happening
* When there’s no spend, the model can intrestingly show that ads impact is growing. Can this be indirect evidence that impact of ads is higher at lower levels of spend?

For example, if you handle a lost item case and follow 🚗 [Rider: I lost a personal item|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360002893034] process, there is an action:
## _Leave a comment on the Order page with the Beehive ticket links, a short description of the issue, and all follow-up actions taken._
# *_In case an automatic comment was already added, should we add further details about the reason behind the refund in the comment?_* _→_ Leaving a comment is not directly tied to refunds. Hi [~accountid:624d3e6c7a3f9e006ab63c88], thank you for raising this. 

The feature of *driver queue optimisation has been flagged by product legal as high risk* in terms of reclassification. This is because when using driver queue optimisation, the historic driver performances are used to “prioritise” or “de-prioritise” a driver in the “dispatch queue”, which may have the effect that “poor performers” will have less access to work as a result of Bolt’s discretion. 

However, the driver queue optimisation feature is _slightly_ less risky than “acceptance rate blocking”. As we are already *using acceptance rate blocking in Sweden, adding this into the mix probably isn't going to change our risk profile dramatically*. 

However, *a full launch will require confirmation from the privacy team* that the data processing involved isn’t considered “highly significant” for the purposes of GDPR etc. Has the privacy team been included in the assessment regarding the driver queue optimisation roll-out in Sweden? 

Thank you! 

Best regards, Emelie

In this circumstance, archiver engine detects that a previous deletion task hadn’t completed properly - it detects the delete had been issued, but no feedback in the cron’s run execution time frame. Hence, the engine skips all the future scheduled tasks with “Postpone the task's execution, the previous context is still running”. It’s expected from the engine’s reliability perspective, but it’s confusing for the end user.  
Action 1 → Pause the job, so that future jobs can be scheduled through Internal API - currently, there is no archive job scheduled by the Internal API because it sees a running job

Action 2 → The archive job to be forcefully stopped with error - ideally with an error description - it’ll be part of the fix provided for this bug.

|*Vague technical safeguards*: Bolt requires that Revolgy explain what its technical safeguards are and if possible, reference them in its DPA. After discussing with [~accountid:62a9b6a7bfade20069655949] about changing the `payment_method_id` to be unique by either switching to UUID v4 or having additional unique ID added as suffix to current id format. We concluded the easiest is to switch to format of: {{companyId-groupId-uniqueId}}.

For data analytics and operations it’s the least disruptive approach as they can still access raw data for their work, while with UUIDs additional complexity is involved by either joining payment methods table or having additional APIs in Admin Panel to decipher the value.

Given that {{payment_method_id}} in database tables is `VARCHAR(255)` field, we have some limitations here but not going to reach them any time soon.

In current format: {{companyId-groupId}} we have limit of {{<128 CHAR companyId>-<127 CHAR groupId>}} . Once we add additional numeric unique id, the constraints look something like this: {{<84 CHAR companyId>-<84 CHAR groupId>-<84 CHAR uniqueId>}}. Obviously IDs don’t balance evenly.

Hi [~accountid:61ae4180ebce470067c8cdc8] - Apologies for the delay on this.

The reason for the mismatch between rider ratings on the App and in Admin is as follows:

* *App*: Average rating is determined by adding together all of the ratings from the last 365 days and dividing the total by 365 (i.e., it is the average for the last year only - see [this article|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/4615013174/Driver+Rating+Rider#Rider-App]).
* *Admin*: Average rating is determined based on the average of all previous ratings ever received (i.e., not just limited to the past 365 days).

As a result, the user’s average rating from the past 365 days (shown in the App) is lower than the user’s average rating over the course of their entire time with Bolt (shown in Admin). We only share the former with the user.

In terms of responding to the user, we are preparing a response and will share it with you as soon as we can.

{quote}🚗 Rider: I was wrongly charged a cancellation fee - Fee was incorrectly applied - Refund actor Driver, only if the driver was at fault (e.g. arrived at the wrong pickup location){quote}

I believe that, as it's written, the agent might be led to interpret it in the following way:

_Ride did not happen because the rider could not find the driver → Cancellation fee should not have applied → Compensate the rider → Refund actor Driver, only if the driver was at fault (e.g. arrived at the wrong pickup location)_ 

Since it doesn't specify whether the driver's failure to answer the phone is the driver's fault, they could interpret it either way and adjust accordingly, with the actor being either the driver or Bolt.

How about adding a more general statement, saying, 

'_if the driver was at the correct pickup point and was eligible for a cancellation fee, the rider should not be compensated for the cancellation fee'_.

Since this is already outlined in the process, I see that some agents may be confused about how to handle these situations. Perhaps a statement like this could help agents better understand how to manage such cases. 🙂

h2. *🌎 User reports pre-authorisation not being released*



Hi Knowledge management team, 



Pre-authorization issues make up ⅕  of all tickets escalated to Commerce service desk. A majority of cases can be solved without the help of the Commerce team. Payment Operations would like to reduce the amount of tickets escalated to the Commerce service desk to reduce the backlog. 

In most cases there aren’t any issues with the pre-authorisation not being released. There is a high number of escalations because the customer lacks visibility over the pre-authorisation process. Most banks do not display the pre-authorisation charges and refunds in the customers bank statement. 

We are requesting some changes to make the process smoother for our customers, CS agents and payment operations. 

To assist your team I have highlighted parts that could be edited in red and added clarifications. 

Please feel free to improve the wording and contact me if additional information is needed. 



# Add context about the release process from [+🥡🥕 Pre-authorisation logic KB+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360019860520] 
# Clarify the payment status section to highlight problematic transactions that are in the *Authorized* state. All of the other states (Captured, Canceled, Failed and Chargeback) are likely not problematic. 
# Update the *Share the pre-authorisation number* section to only provide acquirer reference for *Adyen* transactions. We have found that we are missing the correct references in Admin or the references are not effective at locating the missing funds. 
# The customer support team should escalate the cases to Commerce team only when: 
4.1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank
4.2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 
 



*Release process*

* The pre-auth is usually canceled when the system runs the actual charge. In this case, the payment status changes from _auth_ to _capture_.
* In the unusual event that the eater reports that their pre-auth was not released/returned/canceled, inform them that it can take between 1 to 30 business days, depending on their bank’s release process.
* If after the maximum bank release process time has passed, the eater still has this pending hold on their account, ask them to contact their bank to initiate the release process.

h3. *Step 1: Check the Payment Status*

* {color:#bf2600}Payment Status is: {color}{color:#bf2600}*Authorized and less than 24 hours*{color}{color:#bf2600} have passed, {color}{color:#bf2600}*Canceled*{color}{color:#bf2600}, {color}{color:#bf2600}*Successful*{color}{color:#bf2600} or {color}{color:#bf2600}*Captured*{color}
* If the Status is Captured, Canceled, Failed and Chargeback then most likely the authorized amount has been returned to the customer. 
* If the Status is Authorized and it has been more than 72 hours for Micro mobility then the customer might not be refunded. 
* If the Status is Authorized and it has been more than 24 hours for Delivery and Rides then the customer might not be refunded. 
* {color:#bf2600}Payment Status is: {color}{color:#bf2600}*Authorized and more than 24 hours*{color}{color:#bf2600} have passed{color}
** {color:#bf2600}Escalate to the Commerce team via {color}[{color:#bf2600}+SD+{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/-1]
** {color:#bf2600}Follow the instructions given by the Commerce team{color}

{color:#bf2600}Other cases to escalate to the Commerce team{color}

* {color:#bf2600}The payment error is “gateway timeout” or “client timeout” after 24 hours have passed{color}
* {color:#bf2600}The user has a large number of unreleased pre-authorizations{color}
* {color:#bf2600}You collected data on unreleased pre-authorizations affecting a large number of customers from a specific bank or a country{color}

h3. *Step 2: Share the pre-authorisation number and ask the customer to check with their bank*

How to find the pre-authorization reference number

* For Adyen, it is available as an acquirer reference on the _payment attempts_ page.
** _Payment_ > _Attempts_ > _Authorisation_ > _authorize_ > _search for acquirer reference_
* {color:#bf2600}For PayU, it is the provider transaction ID{color}
** {color:#bf2600}_Payment_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Attempts_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Authorisation_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_authorise_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Response_{color}{color:#bf2600} > search for provider_raw_transaction_id{color}
* {color:#bf2600}For Yigim, RRN{color}
** {color:#bf2600}_Payment_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Attempts_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Authorisation_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_authorise_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Response_{color}{color:#bf2600} > search for rrn{color}
* {color:#bf2600}For Fondy, the approval code{color}
** {color:#bf2600}_Payment_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Attempts_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Authorisation_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_authorise_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Response_{color}{color:#bf2600} > search for approval_code{color}
* {color:#bf2600}For Paystack, authorization reference{color}
** {color:#bf2600}_Payment_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Attempts_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Authorisation_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Metadata_{color}{color:#bf2600} > {color}{color:#bf2600}_Authorisation reference_{color}

Example of the pre-authorization reference number:

!https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXemzrP5tBrc_xS2_lM84JX3CDEOheasV54UMQ_rhkASSZdfbBm5bbJaxQ7PIhBQZ0ud41kS6g71NvatP-5RbCxLXYV9TpaFol6Cdw0vK-_48Vgjlymp-ACB4RtaZnVF1mV3T53NMCaLCKaAo3dbcuJA_V5S?key=DL9HEHAXj_9kisZIaRo42A|width=506,height=36,alt="example"!

* If you found the reference number - share it with the user and advise them to contact their bank
* If there is no reference number - advise the user to contact their bank
** The pre-authorization release duration depends on the rider's bank release process
** The same applies for 3rd party payments (Apple Pay, PayPal, etc.)
* If the user comes back with information from their bank continue to the *Step 3*

h3. {color:#bf2600}*Step 3: Follow up on the issue*{color}

h3. *Step 3: Escalate the issue to Commerce team via SD*

User may return with information from their bank indicating that they should contact us. If _14 days_ have passed since the end of the ride and the bank has directed the user to us:

The Commerce team is able to reach out to our PSPs, trace the funds and provide a trace reference if needed.

Escalate to the Commerce team via [+SD+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/-1] if all of the below requirements have been met:

Answering your questions:

# All the cases were handled by fraud team. When we have a client who has been asked for copy of their ID or passport and they are not happy to do that, we asked them (fraud team) to whitelist the customer, so employees don’t have to send personal documents.
# Tbh with you sending personal documents such as ID or passport is not very well received via our customers or in general in Polish society. So many times IDs or passport were used by people to force a loan, money laundering or to fake documents and sell them illegally.
I read a few comments made by lawyers and some of them are saying that even banks (!!!) should not request scan of ID or passport. Same goes with employer. And I found only those two sectors that are allowed to ask for a scan of someone’s ID or passport.

With scanning personal documents are common cases like: how we storage this data. How long we do so, and what is happening later? How we prevent those data to be stolen by someone outside the company?

Polish act on Identity Cards (IDs) is not directly saying about scanning documents but judicial practice of courts say that only in rare situations other institutions might ask for it, but mostly employer and banks. Even if someone is asking for a scan od ID or passport like Bolt is doing, only the information that is necessary to conclude a specific contract should be reproduced (other confidential information must be covered up).

But now case - we ask for scan of ID or passport users added by admins to business portal (in our case of course). Do we have some regulations about it in our T&Cs we sign with business customers? Plus does Bolt have specific programs for document encryption?



Having everything above I am not sure if we do it fully legally to be honest, or if we do it right. Probably polish legal team have to check everything and tell us if it really is alright or not.

Hope my answers help and we can stop asking people for their IDs.



Have a nice day!

**** If the refund was successful and the rider claims they have not received it still, let them know that it may take {color:#36b37e}at least 14 days{color} for funds to be made available. Recommend the user that they contact their bank for help.

*Current situation:*

* Fleet drivers are currently deleted without notifying fleet owners. 
* Ukraine (and it might be that more markets too) has an internal process that’s not documented - CS escalates the ticket to the local OPS; local OPS reaches out to the fleet owner and confirms if all debts are paid and the driver can be deleted.
* Reaching out to fleet owners before deleting their driver’s profile is relevant to other markets too. Helene Abel shared that there’s an option for fleet owners to mark the “_deactivated”_ button on the driver’s profile. Doing so would make the process faster and won’t require CS escalation to OPS and OPS contacting Fleets. The process could look like this:

Hi! 
I looked into this and while there are general EU requirements that we should keep in mind (as seen below), we will order a legal analysis from a German law firm regarding internal laws.

Therefore we cannot green light this until we have received a legal opinion from the external counsel.

Relevant EU requirements:

Under the EU General Safety Regulation (GSR), all new vehicles registered from July 2024 must include an intelligent speed assistance (ISA). The speed limit feature described in this ticket may be regarded as an ISA. While not all Bolt vehicles fall under the GDR (as they are registered before July 2024) and the GSR itself only applies to manufacturers, it is recommendable to follow the requirements of GSR when implementing such a system. Considering this, these are the main requirements that would need to be followed:

* It must generally be possible to disable the ISA. However, permanent disabling is not permitted. This means that the system is automatically reenabled at the latest once the vehicle has been restarted. DVR recommendation: _It must for example be possible to easily cancel the required speed of the vehicle by normal actuation of the pedal, without the necessity for a kick-down_.
* The ISA must be designed to avoid or at least minimise the error rate under real driving conditions. If high-performance traffic sign recognition is used in combination with GPS data and digital map material, the system should be very reliable.
* It must be made clear to drivers by means of a suitable attention-gaining human-machine interface, that the applicable speed limit has been exceeded. Warning signals should be able to be deactivated or suppressed according to the situation. The visual display of the maximum permissible speed with is detected by the system should not be able to be switched off.

As mentioned above, the implementation of this feature in Germany must wait our external counsel's review. We will update this ticket once this is done.

Initial idea was to add either install from redis-server deb package or redis-stack-server deb.

However, after some tests I noticed these strange decisions they came with for {{redis-stack-server}} package for some reason:

* all stuff is installed to /opt/redis-stack
* running via strange bash wrapper
* owner of service is nobody user instead of redis
* deb package contains temporary files from GH runner
* Most importantly - redis-server is built without systemd support, which leads to issues with systemd handling it
** Message in logs:{{# systemd supervision requested or auto-detected, but Redis is compiled without libsystemd support!}}

So in the end I think it’s easier to repack Redis stack deb into another deb package and keep only modules there and use standard Redis-server deb to deploy redis itself.

I have reviewed the agreement from a FR civil law perspective and the only clause that I would suggest to amend is *Clause 14 termination for breach.* 

Breaches giving the right to the counterparty to terminate needs to be spelled out and only material breaches should give the right to terminate the agreement. Otherwise the failing party should have the right to cure the breach within a specific timeframe*.*

*_Clause 14:_* _if either party breaches any of the obligations under Section(s)_ {color:#ff991f}_[XXXX]_ {color}_of the agreement, the agreement will be terminated within 15 days after the party has received notice from the claiming party. If either party breaches any other term of the agreement, the claiming party will notify the other party providing 15 days from receipt of such a written notice to cure the breach. If the breach is not cured within this period, the claiming party may terminate this agreement within 15 days. Any notice referred hereto must be served in writing to the registered office address, and the party will still be able to claim damages in respect of the breach._

Hey, [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441]! Sorry for the delay. We have discussed the issue of Bolt Send for Business with F&F and there was an issue with delivery documents prescribed by tax legislation. Below is the relevant quote from the email of Rebecca Diacono dated 28.03.24 (you are also in CC to that email):

{quote}we understand that your query related to whether Article 52(2) of the Value Added Tax Act (chapter 406 of the laws of Malta – the “*VATA*”) would apply to courier drivers in the context of Bolt Send-On operations.

Article 52(2), VATA, provides that “_any person who transports goods in the course of an economic activity, on his own behalf or on behalf of or to third parties, shall be in possession at any time of an identification document and a tax invoice or a delivery note or a transport document showing a description of all the goods being transported, the value of the goods, the unit quantity, the date of the delivery, the destination address, the name and address and_ +_value added tax registration number of the supplier and the name and address and value added tax registration number of the person to whom the supply is made_+_...”_ (our emphasis).

Article 52(2), VATA, is drafted in a very wide manner and may arguably apply in the context of any transportation of goods carried out by a person who is delivering the goods in the course of his economic activity. Having said that, it is to be noted that article 52(2), VATA, requires the delivery person to include the VAT number of the supplier and the VAT number of the customer in the relevant document, which would imply that this article was drafted with the intention of applying solely to B2B supplies of goods, (since it is only in such a case that both parties to a supply would be identified by VAT numbers).

We did manage to confirm our interpretation with the VAT Department, who agreed that article 52(2),VATA, should only apply in the context of B2B delivery of goods.{quote}

Therefore, the main problem is that if Bolt Send is used by businesses the driver is required to be in possession of a specific documentation outlining the delivery details. [~accountid:6320602ec7601c8e4abeda47] listed all required data points in his last message. 

We were advised that we will need to amend T&Cs to specifically bring out the requirement to have the required documentation. 

I hope this helps. Please let me know if you have any further questions.

I looked into this and have not identified any legal issues.

Provided that Lynx Cannabis has the necessary permit for producing hemp products (and they follow other requirements of the Lithuanian Hemp Law), their activities should be completely legal. I have not checked whether they have the relevant permit - however, should they not have it, they would be in breach of our T&Cs anyway.

In addition, I have not identified any laws that would apply to Bolt or any other marketplace platform for enabling the sale of hemp products. The hemp specific regulations only regulate the production of hemp products, the supply of hemp products to the market, and the import of hemp products - Bolt would not be doing any of these (supply of fiber hemp products and products to the market is defined as: _holding fiber hemp products and products for sale, including offering for sale or any other means of transfer thereof, free of charge or for money, and the actual sale, distribution and other forms of transfer thereof_).

Therefore there seem to be no legal blocks here and the question falls under Bolt’s preference whether such companies should be allowed on the Lithuania platform or not.

[~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] *to summarise requirements for direct marketing in the UAE:*

*Opt-In Requirement in UAE:* Opt-in consent from users in Dubai and across the UAE is mandatory for sending direct marketing communications.

It cannot be obtained via a privacy notice, and must be separately requested (i.e. via a checkbox).

*Strict consent-record keeping rules for SMS:* Bolt is required to create an SMS consent database and share it with local telecommunications providers [+per this procedure+|https://www.etisalat.ae/en/system/wst/assets/docs/business/general/etisalat-consent-management-service-policy.pdf] to prevent SMS from being blocked.

*Scope of channels:*

* Email
* WhatsApp messages and similar services
* Push notifications
* SMS

*Applicability (at least one criteria must apply):*

* Direct marketing is conducted by a company in the UAE.
* Message is sent to devices located in the UAE.
* Received by Individuals Physically in the UAE at the time of receipt.
* Applicable to both B2C and B2B contexts.

*Enforcement Risk - high*.

* *Likelihood - high.* Authorities actively monitor and are likely to take action, especially in cases of large-scale or repeated violations.
* *Amount of fines* - *not clear, still researched by* [~accountid:712020:a8c9140a-0154-4e85-8d6b-f9d0c371277f] . Based on the publicly available information (unverified), fines can be up to AED 10 million (≈USD 2.7 million).
* *For SMS rules violations specifically -* fines from AED 50,000 to AED 250.000 per violation (up to ≈70 000 USD).

What is IAM User and Roles for S3 bucket:

AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) provides tools to manage access to AWS services and resources securely. Two key concepts within IAM are *IAM Users* and *IAM Roles*:

h3. *IAM User*

* *Definition*: An IAM user is an entity that you create in AWS to represent a person or service that interacts with AWS resources. Each user has specific credentials (like an access key ID and secret access key) that they use to sign in to AWS and make requests to AWS services.
* *Use Cases*: IAM users are typically created for individuals who need access to AWS services. For example, if you have a team of developers, you might create an IAM user for each developer, giving them credentials to access specific AWS resources.
* *Credentials*: IAM users can have login credentials for the AWS Management Console and/or access keys for making API requests to AWS services programmatically.

h3. *IAM Role*

* *Definition*: An IAM role is an AWS identity that you can create with specific permissions. Instead of being associated with a single user, a role is assumed by an entity (like an AWS service, an application, or a user) that needs access to AWS resources temporarily.
* *Use Cases*: IAM roles are useful in situations where you want to grant temporary access to AWS resources without sharing long-term credentials. For example:
** *Cross-Account Access*: An IAM role can be used to allow resources in one AWS account to access resources in another AWS account.
** *Service Roles*: AWS services like EC2 or Lambda can assume a role to perform actions on your behalf.
** *Federated Users*: You can assign roles to users authenticated by an external identity provider (e.g., Google, Microsoft AD) instead of IAM users.

h3. *Key Differences*:

* *Identity vs. Temporary Access*: An IAM user is a long-term identity that has specific permissions. An IAM role is not tied to a single user or service but can be assumed temporarily by different entities.
* *Credentials*: IAM users have permanent credentials (username/password, access keys), while IAM roles use temporary security credentials.
* *Use Case*: IAM users are suited for individual, permanent access, whereas IAM roles are better for temporary, shared, or cross-account access.

h3. *Example Scenario*:

* *IAM User*: A developer needs to access S3 buckets and EC2 instances. You create an IAM user for them, giving them permissions to access these services and providing them with an access key.
* *IAM Role*: You have a Lambda function that needs to read from an S3 bucket. Instead of embedding access keys in your Lambda function, you create an IAM role with the necessary permissions and let the Lambda function assume that role.

In summary, IAM users are best for individual, persistent access needs, while IAM roles are ideal for temporary, flexible access across various AWS services or accounts.

'It turns out that the Lithuanian company (Bolt Service LT UAB) must pay real estate tax on behalf of an individual according to the Lithuanian Real Estate Tax Law (highlighted):

*Real Estate Tax Law, Article 3, Section 3*

*Article 3. Taxpayers*

# The tax is paid by the owners of real estate—natural and legal persons, except in the cases provided for in Sections 2, 3, and 4 of this Article.

*Amendments to the section:*

No. XIII-2244, 2019-06-13, published TAR 2019-06-27, reg. no. 2019-10373

# The tax on real estate being acquired is paid by the natural or legal person acquiring this property if the information about the corresponding transaction is recorded in the public state register.
# The real estate tax for real estate (or part thereof) transferred for an indefinite period or for a period longer than one month to a legal entity, which is owned by a natural person (persons) or is being acquired by him (them), is paid by this legal entity during that period.
# For the owners of real estate in a collective investment entity that is not a legal entity, the person (taxpayer) who fulfills the obligations and exercises the rights established by this law is the management company of that collective investment entity.

*Added section:*

No. XIII-2244, 2019-06-13, published TAR 2019-06-27, reg. no. 2019-10373

*Amendments to the Article:*

No. XI-1158, 2010-11-23, Official Gazette, 2010, No. 145-7415 (2010-12-11); Official Gazette, 2010, No. 154-0 (2010-12-28), reg. no. 1101010ISTA0XI-1158

----

It turns out that the Lithuanian company must also pay and declare income tax when paying A-class income to an individual:

*INCOME TAX CALCULATION, PAYMENT, DECLARATION, AND REFUND PROCEDURE*

*Article 23. The procedure for calculating, withholding, and paying income tax from A-class income*

# A permanent resident of Lithuania, a Lithuanian entity, a permanent establishment, or a non-resident of Lithuania engaged in individual activities through a permanent base, acting as a tax withholding agent, must calculate, withhold, and pay into the budget the income tax specified by this law when paying out payments attributed to A-class income under the tax payment procedure, unless these payments are classified as non-taxable income under the provisions of this law.
# A permanent resident of Lithuania, a Lithuanian entity, a permanent establishment, or a non-resident of Lithuania engaged in individual activities through a permanent base, acting as a tax withholding agent, must pay the withheld income tax into the budget by the 15th of the same month for payments made before the 15th of the relevant tax period, and by the last day of the same month for payments made after the 15th of the relevant tax period.

*Article 24. Declarations of income tax withheld from A-class income*

# The tax withholding agent, who during the tax period paid out payments classified as A-class income, must declare the paid payments, withheld and paid income tax by submitting declarations.
# The declarations of income tax withheld from A-class income are monthly and annual. The monthly declaration, which declares the total amount and, in cases determined by the central tax administrator, the amount of taxable income paid to each resident during that month, and the amount of withheld income tax, must be submitted for each month of the tax period by the 15th of the following month.
# The forms of declarations of income tax withheld from A-class income, as well as the procedure for filling out and submitting the declarations, are established by the central tax administrator. The central tax administrator has the right to establish a list of non-taxable income that is not declared in the declaration of income tax withheld from A-class income, the amount of certain non-taxable income that does not exceed the declared amounts, and additional data provided together with the declaration of income tax withheld from A-class income.

----

All this means that I cannot pay the income tax myself when receiving A-class income from a legal entity, as I would if I were receiving A-class income from a natural person.

Therefore, GPM and real estate tax will not be included in the invoices I issue.

This is how all the companies that have previously rented these premises have acted.

Hi [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] - see the below updates / responses from Teele. In short, we have received a lot (c. 4000) questions / requests over the last year relating to rider ratings. As such, this is clearly an important issue that we should agree an approach on. However, I would still argue that only some of these types of request concern us.

My thoughts on how to respond to this are to reiterate clearly which ones should be escalated to our team to review, and which should not (i.e., in the latter case, we can give CS a standard approach that they can follow). My views on this breakdown are below. {color:#4c9aff}*Can we discuss to make sure we are aligned?*{color}

----

{color:#36b37e}*Issues / Requests / Questions that can be dealt with by CS*{color}

* *I want to know more about my Rider Rating (i.e., requests for* +*general info*+*)* (1627 tickets last year)
** e.g., “_Can you explain to me how rider ratings are calculated?_”
*** +Rationale+: These are not privacy questions. They can also be dealt with quickly.
*** +CS Response+: Refer the rider to the blog post and include a brief explanation (e.g. “_Please note that your Rider Rating as it appears in your Bolt app is calculated as an average rating based on your ratings from the previous 365 days. Each rating is from 1 to 5, as provided by the driver at the end of each trip. Further information on Rider Ratings can be found here:_ [https://bolt.eu/en/rider-rating/|https://bolt.eu/en/rider-rating/|smart-link].”)
* *I want to know why my Rider rating dropped* (1574 tickets last year)
** e.g., “_Hello. I was deducted a point from the rating, please tell me why?_” or “_Why did my rating drop? It was always 5_”
*** +Rationale+: Again, this is not really a privacy question (unless it is raised in the context of data protection law / personal data processing, which these examples are not). These can also be dealt with quickly.
*** +CS Response+: Use a similar response to the above, but also refer to the Marketplace Conduct guidelines ([https://bolt.eu/en/legal/marketplace-guidelines-terms/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/marketplace-guidelines-terms/|smart-link] ) and say that the ratings drop when the drivers rate them (i.e., Bolt cannot control this).
** e.g., “_Rider see her rating differently than we see in admin._”
*** +Rationale+: I am dealing with a similar query from CS ([here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-37847]). The difference is that the app only shows an average rating from the _last 365 days_, which is different to the calculation in Admin. The user would never pick up on this difference, it is just something for CS to be aware of.
*** +CS Response+: N/A. We should just ensure that CS are aware that the rating in admin (which is not visible to the rider) is different to the rating in the app (which is visible to the rider).
* *I want to increase my Rider rating* (805 tickets last year)
** e.g., “_how can we solve the problem of drivers who underestimate the ratings_” or “_it looks like driver had given me a 1* star rating, so it will affect my rating for the future rides. Is that possible to remove its ? All the evidence will be provided if needed_”
*** +Rationale+: Again, this is not really a privacy question. It is also not up to Bolt to manually change rider ratings, as they are at the driver’s discretion, and so these can be dealt with quickly.
*** +CS Response+: Use a similar response to the above, but also refer to the Marketplace Conduct guidelines ([https://bolt.eu/en/legal/marketplace-guidelines-terms/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/marketplace-guidelines-terms/|smart-link] ) and make it clear that ratings are at the driver’s discretion and cannot be controlled by Bolt.

----

{color:#ff5630}*Issues / Requests / Questions that should be escalated to Privacy*{color}

* *Visibility of the Rider Rating*
** e.g. “_Is the passenger rating visible? In this way, you give the drivers the opportunity to give a bad rating to the passengers who reported the rides_” or “_With Bolt I could always see my ratings from the drivers in the app, but that is no longer possible! ! Why is that?_”
*** +Rationale+: I understand that this relates to the outcome of the AKI enquiry. We should therefore carefully control what we say in this regard.
*** +Privacy Response+: TBC (this depends on what we have said to AKI)
* *Requests pertaining to individual ratings*
** e.g., “_What was my rating for this trip_” or “_I would like all the rider ratings ever given to me_”
*** +Rationale+: This is technically a DSAR. Also, I am currently discussing with Tat how we should be responding to these, as there is often a discretionary element in how to respond. As such, this is something privacy should control.
*** +Privacy Response+: TBC (we are discussing this)
* *Issues / requests / questions that explicitly mention either: (a) data protection law; and/or (b) personal data processing*
** e.g., “_How is my personal data processed to calculate my average rating_” or “_I would like you to correct my rider rating per my rights under Article 16 of the GDPR_”
*** +Rationale+: Even if the request itself does not make sense / is nonsense, privacy should review it to double-check, as it falls directly under our remit of expertise.
*** +Privacy Response+: Depends on the request.

Currently there are 3 options to adjust seasonality, listed in order of them being introduced:

# Additive adjustment. Monthly, +5% for September means +5% for all September weeks in all years.
# Multiplicative adjustment. Monthly, 1.2 for September means X * 1.2 for all September weeks in all years.
# Weekly adjustment. Weekly, +5% on single week means +5% on that week only

Seasonality itself is normalized, meaning the total sum is 0. When we’re doing adjustments they’re also should be normalized, so they don’t change total sum after being applied.

Initially we did monthly normalization for additive adjustment, which is not precise, because we work with weeks. Other adjustments have week-based normalization. Now, as we’re retraining all models, we can safely fix this and convert additive adjustments to be weekly-normalized just like 2 other versions.

What it means practically - we have a column BX, which calculates weekly seasonality adjustment. We need the same column (or combine one with BX) for monthly additive adjustments, and seasonality formula in column J should be updated. As a result there will be slight discrepancy with adjusted seasonality and a warning in the training window, but this is fine as it’ll go away after we retrain models

Hi Anusha, following our last discussion, I wanted to confirm that the data regarding refund actors (Bolt/Driver), using a specific driver as an example, has been addressed under question 1. 

1. Why do you think that this does not fall within the realms of Fraud? (you mention that you believe this is service misconduct and not fraud)?

The passenger and Bolt do not always suffer losses. For example, considering the driver 1295429: approximately 82% of refunds are taken from the driver’s balance. 

Fraud typically involves intentional deception for financial gain. Here, the driver’s actions result in poor service levels but do not consistently result in financial loss to Bolt or passengers, as 82% of refunds are taken from the driver’s balance. Since there is no consistent financial loss to Bolt or its users, the service misconduct was considered, rather than fraud.

However, if users do not report the issue, these transactions would go unnoticed, and the driver would receive the money. In about 18% of cases, Bolt is the refunder, and the money is credited to a user (passenger) Bolt's balance. See the data [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZCcAV6DeKZbezf_Rw3kj3XDCr21OMnr9aUw9cwbK_6k/edit?gid=0#gid=0].

Dear Simona,

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 28 July 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular:

* Your passenger invoices for 2023

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/en-mt/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-mt/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*
